assessment: This is a technically compelling study that uses optogenetic methods and rapid flash-and-freeze tissue preservation techniques to provide new insights into how the ribbon synapses of cochlear inner hair cells are able to transmit auditory signals at very high rates. The conclusions of the paper about the mechanisms underlying exocytosis from these synapses are well supported by the data. The findings of this study should be of interest to a broad audience of neurobiologists and sensory physiologists.
